subject: How to get Density per sqkm in Distance package in R

messages.author: 830c5449fd8d3337
messages.subject: How to get Density per sqkm in Distance package in R
parts:
Hi I have started using Package Distance in R environment.
Every thing went fine except I did not get density estimate
here is the attached code
 #fitting distance model ( halfnormal ) to distdata
>  hn.model <-ds(distdata,max(distdata$distance),key ="hn",adjustment =NULL)
Fitting half-normal key function
AIC= 3560.84
No survey area information supplied, only estimating detection function.
> hn.model

Distance sampling analysis object

Detection function:
 Half-normal key function 

Estimated abundance in covered region: 1020.824 
I would like to know what is the "covered region" here, I have given region area as 1, How to get the density estimates/sqkm from this code???
Your help will be appreciated.

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] How to get Density per sqkm in Distance package in R
parts:
Hi Mayank and other listfolk,

If you have set up the data distdata as a flat file (see ?flatfile) then
calling summary on the fitted model will give the density estimates. For
example, with the minke whale data that is bundled with Distance:

> data(minke)
> mm <- ds(minke, truncation=1.5, key="hr", adjustment=NULL)
Fitting hazard-rate key function
AIC= 48.638
> summary(mm)

[[other output omitted]]

Density:
Label Estimate se cv lcl ucl df
1 North 0.01931826 0.007356329 0.3807966 0.008722248 0.04278660 12.96797
2 South 0.04311663 0.010741011 0.2491153 0.025747023 0.07220422 17.96313
3 Total 0.02213734 0.006758467 0.3052971 0.011727174 0.04178857 15.25525

This stratified example for the minke whale data on the distance website
may also be helpful: http://distancesampling.org/R/vignettes/minke.html


best,
--dave
